The *Paṇḍaranāgarājajātaka* (Ja 518) is a canonical story in the Pali Jātaka collection within the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative setting, the Buddha related this story while residing at the Jetavana monastery in Sāvatthī in connection with Devadatta telling a lie and being swallowed up by the earth [SuttaCentral]. In response to the monks' discussion of Devadatta's wrongdoing, the Buddha explained that Devadatta had also told lies and met the same fate of being swallowed by the earth in a previous existence, prompting this narrative of the past [SuttaCentral].
